results.title: Slow websites are frustrating visitors, causing dips in engagement | CX Dive
results.content:
“Frustration and trust are more connected than you might think, so getting that experience right from the first step of the customer journey to the last is critical,” Pitié said.

The rate of frustrating website visits rose nearly 4% year-over-year, according to Contentsquare. JavaScript errors were to blame for the increasing rate of frustrating digital experiences, while page loading times and rage clicks — when a visitor repeatedly clicks an element within 2 seconds — improved year-over-year.

Other measures of frustration — instances when buttons or fields or other elements were clicked multiple times and low page activity — remained flat or slightly decreased. [...] ### Dive Brief:

- Two in 5 customers said they were frustrated by website experiences in 2023, according to a Contentsquare study of more than 3,500 websites and 43 billion site visits, released Wednesday.
- JavaScript errors and pages that loaded slowly were the leading causes of frustration, which Contentsquare defines as specific moments of friction in the online experience.
- “The good news: most of the leading causes of frustration are highly avoidable hurdles,” Jean-Christophe Pitié, chief marketing and partnerships officer at Contentsquare, told CX Dive in an email. Technical issues like slowly loading pages can easily be spotted and addressed, but businesses need to continually monitor the online experiences they’re providing customers, he said.

### Dive Insight: [...] ### Dive Insight:

When a customer’s visit to a website becomes a frustrating experience, its impact can vary greatly, from a momentary inconvenience that distracts a customer to a customer choosing to no longer engage with a site.

“Customers aren't so willing to give second chances, and the universal bounce rate is still hovering around 50%,” Pitié said. “That means one in two customers never make it past the first page of a site."

Brands only have seconds to make a good first impression, he said.

Contentsquare is not alone in its findings. Just over half of consumers say they reduce or stop spending at a business after a very poor experience, according to Qualtrics XM Institute.

results.title: Why Website Visitors Leave Without Contacting You
results.content:
Prioritize the problems that have a clear effect on important customer tasks.

A contact form that cannot be submitted should take priority over a small cosmetic issue.

The same applies to broken appointment links, incorrect phone numbers, and important pages that do not load properly.

Fix the parts that prevent a visitor from completing the task.

Look at unclear service descriptions, missing next-step information, confusing navigation, and unnecessary form questions.

These issues can make a task harder even when the website is technically working.

Test the pages that matter most for your business.

If a key mobile form is difficult to use or a landing page has a major loading problem, that may deserve attention before less important design changes. [...] Imagine someone trying to tap a contact button when a late-loading banner pushes the button down the page.

Unexpected movement can cause frustration and accidental clicks.

Reserve space for images and other elements that load after the initial content.

Service pages, landing pages, contact forms, and booking pages may use different tools or layouts.

Test the pages that actually matter to the customer journey.

Google’s Core Web Vitals guide for business decision makers explains common performance concerns in practical terms.

Before contacting a business, visitors may want to know whether it is real, reliable, and able to provide the service they need.

Trust does not come from adding a large number of badges or making bold claims. [...] It is not realistic to expect every website visit to become a sales lead.

Before changing the website, identify which visitors you actually want to convert and what they are trying to accomplish.

A person who wants to contact your business might give up when:

These are problems the company may be able to improve.

Website analytics can show that a session ended. They cannot automatically tell you why the person left or what they were thinking.

A visitor may have found the answer they needed, planned to return later, or decided the offer was not right for them.

Use analytics to find areas worth investigating, then test those areas rather than treating every exit as proof that something is broken.

Imagine a visitor could leave an itemized receipt explaining the problems they met.

results.content:
# Zozothemes on Facebook: "🚨 Your website is getting visitors, but why aren't they taking action? A great-looking website isn't…"

🚨 Your website is getting visitors, but why aren't they taking action?

A great-looking website isn't enough if visitors can't find what they need or understand what to do next. 👀

Here are 3 common reasons visitors leave your website:

❌ Confusing First Impression Visitors don't understand what you offer.

🐌 Slow & Poor Mobile Experience Slow loading and frustrating navigation drive visitors away.

👉 No Clear Call-to-Action Visitors don't know whether to buy, book, or contact you.

Here's how to improve it:

✅ Communicate your value clearly.
✅ Make your website fast and mobile-friendly.
✅ Add a clear, visible CTA.

Have you ever been to a site where when you click on a link or a menu, instead of taking you to the page you wanted to see, you are taken to somewhere completely random or to a 404 page not found page? Then you have encountered broken links.

Most sites get a few broken links each year from things like articles mentioned in a blog post being deleted or moved, but when they are a part of your site navigation or a link to another page on your website, then they start to annoy customers.

To check if your website has any hidden broken links, go to . This site crawls every link on your website and tests them all to make sure they are working correctly. If you do find any broken links on your site, either delete the link or fix them with the correct link.

results.title: Website Visitor Tracking: Benefits & Types | Salesforce
results.content:
### UX and behavioral mapping

If website visitors constantly drop off on a checkout page, your marketers need to know why. User experience (UX) and behavioral tools generate heatmaps and scroll maps to visualize where users spend the most time on a website or webpage. Tracking this data highlights friction points — like confusing menus or broken links — so teams can optimize the general user journey.
